title: Powers of elements of a finite purely inseparable algebra lie in the base after localization
statement: Let $A'$ be a Noetherian integral domain with fraction field $K'$, and let $E$ be a finite $A'$-algebra [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] that is a domain with fraction field $L$. Assume that $L/K'$ is finite purely inseparable [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. There is a nonzero $s\in A'$ such that, writing $A''=A'[1/s]$ and $E''=E\otimes_{A'}A''$, the following hold: if $K'$ has characteristic $0$, then $E''=A''$; if $K'$ has characteristic $p>0$, then for every $x\in E''$ there is an $n\ge 0$ with $x^{p^n}$ in the image of $A''$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0BR5 (algebra-lemma-purely-inseparable), power calculation for a finite purely inseparable extension and localization

proof.text: Since E is a finite A'-algebra, it is a finitely generated A'-module [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; choose A'-module generators e_1,...,e_r, so every element of E is an A'-linear combination of the e_i. Since L/K' is a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], A' -> K' -> L is injective, so A' -> E is injective and E is a subring of its fraction field L; each e_i lies in L. By the definition [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], in characteristic 0 we have L=K', so e_i=b_i/t_i with b_i,t_i in A', t_i nonzero; in characteristic p>0 there are n_i with e_i^{p^{n_i}} in K', and with N = max n_i also e_i^{p^N}=(e_i^{p^{n_i}})^{p^{N-n_i}} in K', say e_i^{p^N}=b_i/t_i with b_i,t_i in A', t_i nonzero. Put s = t_1...t_r, nonzero since A' is a domain. Then A''=A'[1/s] is a subring of K', E''=E[1/s] is a subring of L (localization of a domain at a nonzero element), and the image of A'' in E'' is A'' itself; in characteristic 0 each e_i lies in A'', in characteristic p each e_i^{p^N} lies in A''.

source.place: Algebra, Section 0BR5 (algebra-section-universal-homeomorphism): finite-algebra spreading input for Lemma 0BR8 (algebra-lemma-powers); the argument here is the elementary denominator clearing

proof.text: In characteristic 0, step 1 gives e_i in A'' for every module generator e_i, so E''=sum A'' e_i is contained in A''; the reverse inclusion is the structure map A''->E'', which is injective by step 1. Hence E''=A''.

source.place: Algebra, Section 0BR5 (algebra-section-universal-homeomorphism): finite-algebra spreading input for Lemma 0BR8 (algebra-lemma-powers); the argument here is the elementary denominator clearing

proof.text: Assume characteristic p>0. The e_i generate E'' as an A''-module, so every x in E'' is x=sum a_i e_i with a_i in A''. Since the Frobenius y -> y^{p^N} is a ring endomorphism in characteristic p, x^{p^N}=sum a_i^{p^N} e_i^{p^N}, and by step 1 each e_i^{p^N} lies in A''; hence x^{p^N} lies in the image of A''. Thus every x in E'' has a p-power in the base, with the uniform exponent n=N.

proof.text: Localization preserves the displayed fraction-field identification: A'' has fraction field K' and E'' has fraction field L, since s is nonzero and E is a domain finite over A'. Therefore the two characteristic cases establish all clauses of the statement.
